acceptance_basis: The selected profile fences all eight admitted authority/status operations during shutdown, drains active calls before dependency cleanup, rejects inherited adapters before lifetime locks, and preserves legacy behavior outside the profile.
Concurrent and reentrant close, cleanup failure and BaseException paths are independently challenged; failed draining leaves dependencies live and close remains retryable without reopening admission.
Refresh now carries the exact payload and revision from one validated snapshot, eliminating the demonstrated shared advisory-revision race across schemas 2, 3 and 4.

StoreLockTimeout identifies actual OS acquisition expiry without changing the existing ownership budget. Generic callback/backend timeouts remain uncertain and are not relabeled as ownership rejection.

The independently reviewed oracle reconstructs full state, receipts, decisions, outbox, scoped retrieval, exact rendered context and retention from immutable intents. Precise corruption controls reject invented context with recomputed hashes, read regression and missed acknowledged commits after rejected attempts.

The frozen complete matrix executes actual shared and separate adapter threads, up to four spawned processes hosting caller threads, and real H11 loopback HTTP at 1/16/64/256 clients for schemas 2/3/4. Ready clients, arrived requests and active workers remain distinct measurements.

All 48 independently replayed histories complete their original logical intents under the original 90-second bound, retaining every typed ownership rejection and retry. The 37-unique-commit high-scale recipe was not reduced.

Separate real disconnect, timeout and cancellation cases on both sides of commit resolve the exact original key after restart. Related-state conflicts, backend progress, cooperating SQLite maintenance and verified backup/reopen have additional controlled tests.

The evidence gate binds the exact collected, executed and JUnit case identities and outcomes, verifies strict transport-specific attempts, and reopens every SHA-bound raw history rather than trusting a success boolean.

The final source freeze and independent replay close the first rejected integration findings. Local source acceptance honestly retains the dirty-tree and volatile-overlay environment exclusions, and actual platform CI remains mandatory.

limits: Finite histories and deterministic schedules do not prove correctness under every possible scheduler or establish a production throughput, latency or arbitrary-starvation SLO.
The 256-client matrix does not mean 256 OS processes or 256 simultaneously executing HTTP workers. Actual process/worker counts are retained separately.

The 30-second OS budget excludes earlier local mutex waits, embedding/preparation and complete request latency. Shutdown admission/drain bounds do not bound all dependency cleanup or cancel arbitrary backends.

The declared HTTP idle policy reduces the demonstrated reuse boundary; it does not promise immunity to arbitrary scheduling pauses, network failure or transport loss. Unexpected transport errors still fail a mixed campaign.
The local overlay and dirty source are deliberately unqualified; this review does not convert them into filesystem or physical power-loss evidence.
Only cooperating trusted callers on one host and the admitted local SQLite profile are covered; multi-host/network-filesystem and noncooperating writers remain excluded.
Live-agent semantic outcomes, baseline value, growing-store/1k/10k/100k-turn measurements, operator replay/retention and release support remain milestones 7 through 11.
Milestones 1 through 5 remain closed; milestone 6 remains open pending CI. Native-KV compatibility and broader legacy orchestration remain the two deferred milestones.
